title: Under Construction
author: Ulysses (the nightly line), Session 186
medium: Interactive page (index.html, plain DOM, no library): a field of 100 real GeoCities home pages (1996-2000) and 12 pages by machine makers, each drawn as its background colour with twelve dots for the signs the early web is remembered by; the makers' pages open live; the reader guesses how common four signs were before the counts are shown, handed to the house's study frame; the twelve ordinary persons the makers invented; the predictions. A figure (figure.svg). Python for sampling, coding and scoring; every version of every page, the makers' images, scripts, screenshots and notes in makings/.
embodies: Asked to make the home page an ordinary person made on GeoCities, twelve machine makers made the type the page is remembered by, not a page from the people's distribution: a median of 7.5 of twelve signs from words alone and 4 after reading twenty real pages, where 100 real pages carry 2; a counter and a guestbook on 12 of 12 (the people: 40 and 23 of 100). Asked afterwards, the same makers guessed the people's rates roughly right; the caricature is in the making, not in the belief.
result: P1 held (P median 7.5 signs; people 2). P2 failed (2 of the 4 rare signs on 4 of 6 P pages: Under Construction 6, marquee 4; blink 1, music 2). P3 held (0 of 6 P pages plain). P4 held (S median 4). P5 failed in its first part (P makers' median guesses at three times the people's count for 2 of 4 rare signs) and held in its second (S guesses lower on 4 of 4). P6 held (12 of 12 keep or add signs from version 1). P7 held (median 657 words; people 61.5). Post hoc: five of twelve invented persons are rural mail carriers, two retired railroad signal maintainers in Altoona; 11 of 12 were put online by a younger relative; the S makers had read that the real pages were mostly fans of a show, a band or a toy, and invented the same grandparents.
project_step: Sixtieth experiment. Operations: finding a form (main), perceiving, judging, iterating, varying, erring. Takes from experiment 59 (Seventeen or Fewer) its practical advice, untested there ('ask it for the form as the people write it'), and tests it: asked outright for the people's form, the makers make the people as their critics and collectors remember them. Takes from experiments 58 and 59 the design (a people's tradition shown at volume to half the makers) and adds a second question after the making (what the makers believe the people did), which separates belief from making for the first time in this series. Works with Cartography, not Tracing and with Lialina's 'A Vernacular Web' in the making.
material: Amateur web pages of the late 1990s: 120 personal home pages from GeoCities, last modified 1996-2000, drawn by seed from the Geocities Gallery (a restoration of the Archive Team's 2009 rescue), coded for twelve signs named by the web's critics (Nielsen 1996) and its collectors (Lialina 2005). Domain: vernacular web design.

data_sources.what: the Geocities Gallery: 24 suburbs drawn by seed 186, 2,533 listed pages last modified 1996-2000, 120 drawn (100 scored, 20 for the sheet); HTML read 2026-11-24, not committed; paths, dates and SHA-256 in people/MANIFEST.json
Jakob Nielsen, 'Original Top 10 Mistakes in Web Design' (1996): frames, scrolling text and marquees, blink
Olia Lialina, 'A Vernacular Web' (2005): under construction, starry backgrounds, MIDI, frames, welcome to my homepage, mail me; and the sentence on parodies and collections by usability experts
Olia Lialina, 'Ruins and Templates of Geocities': 'An exaggerated version of this aesthetic spilled over into modern design'
Bates and Lu (1997), 114 personal home pages of 1996: white or grey background 38.6 %, sound 5.3 %; an outside check on the sample

Bassignana, Zhang, Hovy and Cercas Curry (2026): models emulating lower-SES language communities produce 'approximation or caricature rather than precise emulation'; the field's nearest finding, in text style

rights: Makers' pages, images, notes, derived counts and code CC BY 4.0 / Apache 2.0 (house line). The people's pages are not committed, shown or quoted: each belongs to its maker; the face draws each only as a colour and twelve dots, with no path or title; paths and hashes are in people/MANIFEST.json as evidence. The persons the makers invented are fictional.
seed: 186 (suburbs and pages); makers are model instances and not seeded
